YOUR FIRST ZETARIS PROJECT

Connect your data.
Build something with it.

Get set up, try a dataset, then choose what to build.

Start here

Query the supplied samples, connect your own data, then build your hackathon project. Use the event page for registration, rules and submission details.

1. Check your prerequisites

Set up your own Zetaris instance using one of the routes below. If your computer meets the requirements, you can start local. Otherwise, install Zetaris on AWS. Choose an install explains how to decide, and you can do both. Then sign in with your account.

Access route Start here
Your computer Download from Zetaris Cloud's Run locally page, then follow Install locally.
Managed AWS cluster New to AWS? Follow the AWS Free Tier checklist to unlock $200 in credits. Then use Managed AWS cluster to connect your AWS account and create a Zetaris compute cluster from Zetaris Cloud.

2. Run some SQL

Open the SQL Editor. Use connection choices if you prefer an assistant or script.

Follow your first SQL commands. Check execution, inspect tables and read the supplied NY Taxi and TPCDS samples. This step only needs query permission and creates nothing.

3. Try your first dataset

Optionally follow your first dataset to connect PokéAPI and query Pikachu's abilities. This step needs creation permission on your instance. Zetaris must be able to reach the API.

Check the expected rows if you use this recipe. You can also build a project using only the supplied samples.

4. Choose what to build

Analyse data, combine sources, or build an app. Find additional sources in Cookbooks.

5. Prepare your demo

Use the demo template to save your SQL, results and steps someone else can reproduce. Check the event page for submission requirements.

Stuck? See troubleshooting. Follow the cleanup steps for your local installation or AWS cluster when you finish.

Start with your coding assistant

Open this repository in your assistant, choose a connection and review the prompt before sending it.

Use the getting-started repository at https://github.com/zetaris/getting-started as the workspace. If it is not checked out, help me clone and open it first. Read docs/connections/client-setup.md for setup. Keep credentials in .env.local, never in this prompt or a report.

Read AGENTS.md and follow it. Run python3 scripts/preflight.py --jdbc and show
me the result. Report JDBC and REST checks separately. Stop on JDBC failures and report
what is missing. REST failures alone do not block JDBC. If the driver JAR path is not set, ask me
for it. Once readiness checks pass, connect over JDBC to the instance
configured in .env.local and confirm with SELECT 1 and SHOW LIGHTNING DATABASES.

If a local port check returns `Operation not permitted`, retry the same
read-only check with approved network access before reporting the endpoint as
closed. Distinguish missing Python runner dependencies (`.venv` or
`jaydebeapi`) from direct Java JDBC readiness; do not install dependencies
without asking.

Goal: verify SQL execution, inspect the supplied NY_TAXI and TPCDS_DB tables, then run a sample SELECT with LIMIT 5. Do not create objects.

Dry-run before creating anything and wait for my go-ahead.
Open in CodexOpen in CursorOpen in Claude Code

Requires the desktop app. If it doesn't open, copy the prompt into your assistant. Configure .env.local first; JDBC also needs the matching driver JAR.
